questions.q: Data on the sheet: CO₂ volume every 30 s for 1 M and 2 M HCl with marble chips. (a) Mean rate for 2 M over the first 60 s [2]. (b) Sketch both curves and label [2]. (c) Explain the difference using collision theory [3]. (d) Why do both curves level off at the same volume when the acid is in excess? [1]
questions.a: (a) e.g. 54 ÷ 60 = 0.9 cm³/s (2); (b) 2 M steeper, same final volume (2); (c) more acid particles per volume (1), more frequent collisions (1), so faster rate (1); (d) the same mass of marble (limiting reactant) is used up (1)
questions.model: Teacher reads the data table and sets out (a).

questions.q: Explain why raising temperature by 10 °C can roughly double the rate.
questions.a: Particles move faster/more kinetic energy (1); more frequent collisions (1); a much bigger fraction have energy ≥ activation energy (1)

questions.q: Draw a reaction profile with and without a catalyst and label activation energy.
questions.a: Lower hump for catalysed path; same start and end energies

questions.q: Explain why powdered marble reacts faster than chips.
questions.a: Larger surface area (1), so more frequent collisions between acid particles and marble (1)
questions.model: Powder exposes more particles. More exposed particles, more collisions per second. More collisions, faster rate.

questions.q: How can you show a catalyst is unchanged?
questions.a: Weigh it before and after (1); same mass/filter and dry it (1)
